- 'Healthy Net debt equity ratio at 0.16x as on June 30, 2026 as compared to 0.11x as on March 31, 2026' and 'Gross debt equity ratio at 0.27x as on June 30, 2026 as compared to 0.25x as on March 31, 2026' — leverage rose sequentially in the quarter.

bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Single-segment focus on buildings: 'We work in one segment: buildings. That focus is the source of our depth' - systems, site experience, prequalifications and client relationships deepen with each project, making the position harder to replicate
- Complexity advantage - builds towers of 80 floors and above on constrained urban sites where engineering, sequencing, safety, manpower, materials and timelines demand close control
- Scale record of delivery - 100+ projects, 70+ clients and more than 75 million sq. ft. of constructed area over the past decade
- Integrated EPC delivery framework combining design coordination, construction expertise and project management under one roof, spanning shell-and-core through complete lock-and-key and MEP
- Long-standing clientele relationships with leading public institutions, urban development bodies, infrastructure agencies and prominent private developers, reflecting prequalification strength
- Horizontal Prudence discipline - project selection, working capital, funding cost, order quality and asset use are managed as an explicit counterweight to growth
- Credit standing improved during and after FY26, with long-term bank facility and NCD ratings upgraded to IVR BBB/Stable and subsequently to IVR BBB+/Stable
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Working capital intensity and receivables — Construction projects require significant upfront mobilisation and involve extended collection cycles; management flags that 'Elevated receivables and WC days (152 days) remain a focus area' and is executing a structured receivables reduction plan targeting WC days of 90 over 2.5 years, with legal and commercial escalation mechanisms for delayed payments. Growth-linked working capital was the primary driver of the elevated debt level versus the prior year.
- Geographic concentration in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region — Approximately 72% of the order book is concentrated in MMR, creating dependence on the economic and regulatory environment of a single geography. Mitigation is a gradual reduction in MMR concentration and active pursuit of projects in other geographies that meet internal project selection criteria.
- Labour availability and skilled workmen shortage — Construction is labour-intensive and a shortage of skilled and semi-skilled workers could hit project timelines and cost structures, particularly in peak execution phases. The captive Labour Resource Department, a registered workmen database, structured onboarding, a 15-day wage cycle (faster than the industry monthly standard) and the eFORCE workmen management app are the stated mitigations.
- Financing structure - high-cost NCDs and contingent liabilities — Outstanding NCDs represent elevated financing costs relative to bank debt, and contingent liabilities plus ongoing working capital intensity could pressure credit metrics if cash collections slow. The Company is progressively retiring high-cost NCDs as cash flows improve, targeting a healthier debt mix over the medium term; credit ratings were upgraded from IVR BBB-/Stable to IVR BBB/Stable in August 2025 and further to IVR BBB+/Stable in May 2026.
- Regulatory and environmental interruption to execution — NGT-directed site stoppages, RERA-related regulatory requirements and local body approvals can create project execution delays beyond management control. Compliance teams are deployed at each site with dedicated RERA and legal cells and regularly audited site HSE protocols.
- Competitive intensity in the EPC market — The EPC market is highly competitive, with multiple organised and regional players bidding for large government and private projects, which can pressure margins and order intake. Differentiation rests on exclusive focus on building and factory construction, deep technical expertise in formwork systems and relationships with marquee clients.
- Occupational health and safety at construction sites — Identified as a material risk in the BRSR because the Company operates in high-risk environments involving work at height, machinery, confined spaces and hazardous materials; non-compliance can lead to injuries, fatalities, legal penalties and project delays, while fewer incidents enhance trust, retention and project performance.
- Climate change resilience and weather disruption — Construction is exposed to climate risks including heatwaves, flooding and heavy rainfall, causing project delays and cost overruns; monsoon planning, material protection and safer sequencing are the stated site-level responses.

outlook.body:
- The Company's stated policy intent is that dividend decisions are taken on the basis of profits, cash needs and growth plans, governed by a board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy that sits alongside the Related Party Transaction, CSR, Nomination and Remuneration, Risk Management and Board Diversity policies. Capital discipline is framed as 'Horizontal Prudence' - grip on project selection, working capital, funding cost and asset use - and the stated FY27 governance priority is to 'maintain project selection quality, improve cash conversion and strengthen risk monitoring'. Balance-sheet posture is conservative on external funding: the Company has not accepted any deposits from the public or otherwise during FY26, and lender confidence improved as credit ratings for long-term bank facilities and Non-Convertible Debentures were upgraded to IVR BBB/Stable (short-term IVR A3+) during FY26 and further to IVR BBB+/Stable and IVR A2 after year-end, reaffirmed on May 19, 2026. The Board reported no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position between the end of FY26 and the date of the Report, and CSR spend was made at the statutorily required level of at least 2% of average net profits of the preceding three financial years. Board oversight of capital is exercised through the Audit Committee, the Risk Management Committee and a dedicated Finance and Operation Committee chaired by the Executive Chairman.
- Eleven material ESG topics identified for FY26: occupational health and safety, climate change resilience, waste management, human rights and labour conditions, energy efficiency, water management, employee and workforce wellbeing, sustainable procurement, data security, innovation in green building practices, and regulatory compliance
- BRSR FY26 reporting aligned to GRI Standards (GRI 2 General Disclosures, GRI 2-29 stakeholder engagement, GRI 3 Material Topics) and to UN SDGs 8, 11, 16 and 17; prepared through a technology-enabled online reporting platform. No external assessment or assurance provider was engaged for FY26
- FY27 Environment priorities: improve measurement of energy, water and waste; reduce avoidable material wastage; widen use of efficient construction systems
- FY27 Safety priorities: strengthen training, reporting, audits and closure of observations, supported by a comprehensive HSE framework with mandatory safety inductions, PPE protocols, regular safety audits and incident reporting, benchmarked to institutional client requirements such as CIDCO and MHADA, with safety metrics forming part of project KPIs
- FY27 People priorities: improve workmen facilities, technical training and young engineer development; structured skills development covering core construction skills, safety awareness and specialised formwork operation, plus leadership development to build a pipeline of project managers and site heads
- FY27 Supply chain priorities: improve vendor review, procurement timing and compliance checks; FY27 Community priority: link CSR projects to measurable outcomes
- Worker welfare as an ESG lever: workmen paid on a 15-day wage cycle, significantly faster than the industry standard monthly cycle, which reduces financial stress on labour and improves retention and morale; employee welfare covers group insurance, health and medical support and an Employee Assistance Programme
- Board gender diversity: 2 of 8 Board members are women, representing 25% female representation at the highest governance level
- Grievance and redressal mechanisms maintained for all stakeholder categories - employees, workers, value chain partners, investors and shareholders - with dedicated channels and publicly accessible web links, plus a vigil mechanism and Whistle Blower Policy
- CSR focused on the communities in which the Company operates with emphasis on construction workmen and their families - skill development and vocational training for underprivileged youth, health camps and medical check-ups at project sites and nearby communities, educational support for children of workmen, and site-level environmental initiatives including waste reduction and clean surroundings programmes, overseen by the CSR Committee

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no discrete plant, capacity or rupee-value capex programme - Capacit'e is a contract-led EPC builder rather than an asset-capacity business, so expansion is expressed as geographic and vertical reach rather than commissioning timelines. The Company operates a focussed EPC model from its Mumbai headquarters and has constructed more than 75 million sq. ft. across major Indian cities since inception in 2012, executing high-rise and super high-rise residential work at scale across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, NCR, Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad, and extending the same structural capability into commercial buildings (office complexes, malls and retail, multi-level car parks, hotels) as well as healthcare, education, hospitality, data centre and factory infrastructure. Management frames growth as 'Vertical Dominance. Horizontal Prudence' - pursuing larger and more complex mandates while holding discipline over project selection, working capital, funding cost, order quality and asset use, and states it continues to sharpen systems, strengthen project selection and improve resource deployment so it can 'pursue larger opportunities while protecting the fundamentals'. The only dated corporate expansion action in these sections is a Special Resolution proposed at the 14th AGM (scheduled July 24, 2026) to alter Clause 3(A)(1) of the Main Objects of the Memorandum of Association to expressly include construction and development of buildings such as residential, commercial and institutional - widening the chartered scope of activity.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's construction sector extended its growth momentum in FY26 on structural tailwinds from urbanisation, rising government capital expenditure and recovering private developer activity; it contributes approximately 9% of GDP and employs over 71 million workers
- The Engineering, Procurement and Construction segment recorded revenue growth of 15 to 18% during the year, advancing from the 12 to 15% growth of FY25
- Industry operating margins improved to between 12.5 and 13.5%, supported by stable raw material prices, disciplined project bidding among leading players and continued execution efficiency gains
- India's construction market, valued at approximately USD 0.79 trillion, is projected to expand to USD 1.10 trillion by 2031, cementing its position as the third-largest construction market globally
- Public capital expenditure remains the most consequential demand driver: ₹12.2 lakh crore was allocated in FY26 and the Union Budget for FY27 maintained the trajectory with capital allocation estimated at USD 130 billion, alongside an Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund
- Urbanisation demand base - India is expected to add over 300 million new urban residents over the next three decades, creating durable large-scale demand for housing, commercial space, urban infrastructure and institutional facilities
- A second wave of real estate demand is building beyond the metros across nine emerging cities (Chandigarh Tricity, Lucknow, Jaipur, Indore, Nagpur, Coimbatore, Kochi, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati) where operating costs run 25 to 50% below Tier 1 benchmarks
- Affordable housing is a structural gap - a shortage of approximately 10 million homes with demand projected to reach 30 million units by 2030, supported by housing finance outstanding projected to grow from USD 379.7 billion to USD 932.3 billion by FY 2030
- Government programmes deepen the pipeline: PMAY-U 2.0 (central assistance of ₹2.30 lakh crore for 2024 to 2030), SWAMIH Fund 2 (₹15,000 crore corpus), the ₹1 lakh crore Urban Challenge Fund expected to catalyse nearly ₹4 lakh crore of urban-sector investment over five years, AMRUT 2.0 (₹77,640 crore outlay) and PM-ABHIM health infrastructure construction
- Seven high-speed rail corridors were approved in FY27 and 50-year interest-free capital loans to states (₹1.5 lakh crore allocated in FY26) are broadening the geographic spread of construction activity beyond the metros
- Green and sustainable construction is becoming a commercial condition rather than a reputational gesture - institutional occupiers and ESG-conscious investors increasingly require green certification for long-term lease commitments, and India's green buildings market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% to reach USD 85 billion by FY 2032
- Digital capability is becoming a qualification condition - leading contractors serving large institutional and commercial clients are now expected to demonstrate BIM capability as a standard qualification condition, with AI-based predictive analytics deployed for schedule risk, procurement optimisation and site safety
- Advanced formwork and automation (automatic climbing systems, aluminium formwork, table formwork, composite panels, drones, IoT/telematics) are improving construction speed, dimensional accuracy and equipment utilisation, and gradually addressing labour availability constraints in high-rise work
- Industry-level, not company-specific: 'Industry order books stood at approximately 4.0 times annual revenue at year-end, providing strong near-term visibility.'
- The construction capex pipeline spans national highways, urban mass transit, railway modernisation, affordable housing, institutional infrastructure, logistics parks, data centres and industrial facilities, across both public and private sector

deepdive.thesis: Capacit'e delivered resilient Q4/FY26 execution despite labor disruptions and commodity spikes, provisioning INR 10cr for input costs while guiding 20% revenue growth for FY27 backed by a record INR 13,498cr order book. risks.note: Construction projects require significant upfront mobilisation and involve extended collection cycles; management flags that 'Elevated receivables and WC days (152 days) remain a focus area' and is executing a structured receivables reduction plan targeting WC days of 90 over 2.5 years, with legal and commercial escalation mechanisms for delayed payments. Growth-linked working capital was the primary driver of the elevated debt level versus the prior year.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region
risks.note: Approximately 72% of the order book is concentrated in MMR, creating dependence on the economic and regulatory environment of a single geography. Mitigation is a gradual reduction in MMR concentration and active pursuit of projects in other geographies that meet internal project selection criteria.

risks.risk: Labour availability and skilled workmen shortage
risks.note: Construction is labour-intensive and a shortage of skilled and semi-skilled workers could hit project timelines and cost structures, particularly in peak execution phases. The captive Labour Resource Department, a registered workmen database, structured onboarding, a 15-day wage cycle (faster than the industry monthly standard) and the eFORCE workmen management app are the stated mitigations.

risks.risk: Financing structure - high-cost NCDs and contingent liabilities
risks.note: Outstanding NCDs represent elevated financing costs relative to bank debt, and contingent liabilities plus ongoing working capital intensity could pressure credit metrics if cash collections slow. The Company is progressively retiring high-cost NCDs as cash flows improve, targeting a healthier debt mix over the medium term; credit ratings were upgraded from IVR BBB-/Stable to IVR BBB/Stable in August 2025 and further to IVR BBB+/Stable in May 2026.

risks.risk: Regulatory and environmental interruption to execution
risks.note: NGT-directed site stoppages, RERA-related regulatory requirements and local body approvals can create project execution delays beyond management control. Compliance teams are deployed at each site with dedicated RERA and legal cells and regularly audited site HSE protocols.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity in the EPC market
risks.note: The EPC market is highly competitive, with multiple organised and regional players bidding for large government and private projects, which can pressure margins and order intake. Differentiation rests on exclusive focus on building and factory construction, deep technical expertise in formwork systems and relationships with marquee clients.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's construction sector extended its growth momentum in FY26 on structural tailwinds from urbanisation, rising government capital expenditure and recovering private developer activity; it contributes approximately 9% of GDP and employs over 71 million workers
- The Engineering, Procurement and Construction segment recorded revenue growth of 15 to 18% during the year, advancing from the 12 to 15% growth of FY25
- Industry operating margins improved to between 12.5 and 13.5%, supported by stable raw material prices, disciplined project bidding among leading players and continued execution efficiency gains
- India's construction market, valued at approximately USD 0.79 trillion, is projected to expand to USD 1.10 trillion by 2031, cementing its position as the third-largest construction market globally
- Public capital expenditure remains the most consequential demand driver: ₹12.2 lakh crore was allocated in FY26 and the Union Budget for FY27 maintained the trajectory with capital allocation estimated at USD 130 billion, alongside an Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund
- Urbanisation demand base - India is expected to add over 300 million new urban residents over the next three decades, creating durable large-scale demand for housing, commercial space, urban infrastructure and institutional facilities
- A second wave of real estate demand is building beyond the metros across nine emerging cities (Chandigarh Tricity, Lucknow, Jaipur, Indore, Nagpur, Coimbatore, Kochi, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati) where operating costs run 25 to 50% below Tier 1 benchmarks
- Affordable housing is a structural gap - a shortage of approximately 10 million homes with demand projected to reach 30 million units by 2030, supported by housing finance outstanding projected to grow from USD 379.7 billion to USD 932.3 billion by FY 2030
- Government programmes deepen the pipeline: PMAY-U 2.0 (central assistance of ₹2.30 lakh crore for 2024 to 2030), SWAMIH Fund 2 (₹15,000 crore corpus), the ₹1 lakh crore Urban Challenge Fund expected to catalyse nearly ₹4 lakh crore of urban-sector investment over five years, AMRUT 2.0 (₹77,640 crore outlay) and PM-ABHIM health infrastructure construction
- Seven high-speed rail corridors were approved in FY27 and 50-year interest-free capital loans to states (₹1.5 lakh crore allocated in FY26) are broadening the geographic spread of construction activity beyond the metros
- Green and sustainable construction is becoming a commercial condition rather than a reputational gesture - institutional occupiers and ESG-conscious investors increasingly require green certification for long-term lease commitments, and India's green buildings market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% to reach USD 85 billion by FY 2032
- Digital capability is becoming a qualification condition - leading contractors serving large institutional and commercial clients are now expected to demonstrate BIM capability as a standard qualification condition, with AI-based predictive analytics deployed for schedule risk, procurement optimisation and site safety
- Advanced formwork and automation (automatic climbing systems, aluminium formwork, table formwork, composite panels, drones, IoT/telematics) are improving construction speed, dimensional accuracy and equipment utilisation, and gradually addressing labour availability constraints in high-rise work
- Industry-level, not company-specific: 'Industry order books stood at approximately 4.0 times annual revenue at year-end, providing strong near-term visibility.'

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections disclose no discrete plant, capacity or rupee-value capex programme - Capacit'e is a contract-led EPC builder rather than an asset-capacity business, so expansion is expressed as geographic and vertical reach rather than commissioning timelines. The Company operates a focussed EPC model from its Mumbai headquarters and has constructed more than 75 million sq. ft. across major Indian cities since inception in 2012, executing high-rise and super high-rise residential work at scale across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, NCR, Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad, and extending the same structural capability into commercial buildings (office complexes, malls and retail, multi-level car parks, hotels) as well as healthcare, education, hospitality, data centre and factory infrastructure. Management frames growth as 'Vertical Dominance. Horizontal Prudence' - pursuing larger and more complex mandates while holding discipline over project selection, working capital, funding cost, order quality and asset use, and states it continues to sharpen systems, strengthen project selection and improve resource deployment so it can 'pursue larger opportunities while protecting the fundamentals'. The only dated corporate expansion action in these sections is a Special Resolution proposed at the 14th AGM (scheduled July 24, 2026) to alter Clause 3(A)(1) of the Main Objects of the Memorandum of Association to expressly include construction and development of buildings such as residential, commercial and institutional - widening the chartered scope of activity.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Single-segment focus on buildings: 'We work in one segment: buildings. That focus is the source of our depth' - systems, site experience, prequalifications and client relationships deepen with each project, making the position harder to replicate
- Complexity advantage - builds towers of 80 floors and above on constrained urban sites where engineering, sequencing, safety, manpower, materials and timelines demand close control
- Scale record of delivery - 100+ projects, 70+ clients and more than 75 million sq. ft. of constructed area over the past decade
- Integrated EPC delivery framework combining design coordination, construction expertise and project management under one roof, spanning shell-and-core through complete lock-and-key and MEP
- Long-standing clientele relationships with leading public institutions, urban development bodies, infrastructure agencies and prominent private developers, reflecting prequalification strength
- Horizontal Prudence discipline - project selection, working capital, funding cost, order quality and asset use are managed as an explicit counterweight to growth
- Credit standing improved during and after FY26, with long-term bank facility and NCD ratings upgraded to IVR BBB/Stable and subsequently to IVR BBB+/Stable

risks.body: Geopolitical conflict driving commodity prices (Aluminum, Copper, Fuel) higher than escalation indices; Labor availability shortages (short ~3,000 workers currently, total requirement ~14,000); Environmental stoppages (GRAP in NCR, NGT orders); Election-related disruptions (already factored for FY27); Client slowdown in Tier-2/3 cities if construction costs rise sharply.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
